editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在优雅与局限之间：一本新的图集展现了前东欧集团的社会主义酒店建筑。这些照片见证了一种在今天已经罕见的审美约束力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在“一切皆有可能的后元现代主义”（Anything-goes-Post-Metamoderne）和在广大全球范围内大行其道的晚期资本主义中（而这并未自动带来它曾经承诺的自由主义优势），人们对具有约束力的审美的渴望非常强烈。埃莱娜·阿马比利（Elena Amabili）与卡罗琳·埃登（Caroline Eden）在社会主义中找到了这种美。更准确地说，是在其旅游建筑中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《社会主义酒店》（Socialist Hotels）系列汇集了从阿布哈兹到乌兹别克斯坦以及其间所有国家的典范：格鲁吉亚、阿尔巴尼亚、拉脱维亚、立陶宛、乌克兰、俄罗斯、摩尔多瓦、波兰、罗马尼亚和塞尔维亚。前德意志民主共和国（东德）也由几个例子代表；不过那里的酒店早已荒废。从这些精选作品中涌现出一种出乎意料的丰富性，现已结集成书出版。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正是这种局限性与大都市优雅气息的特殊结合，赋予了许多被介绍的建筑至今仍具吸引力的魅力。某些全景大堂完全可以作为加州群山中西方世纪中叶现代主义（Midcentury-Moderne）的招牌。当然，其他一些曾经的庞大酒店看起来则没有那么大方，在莫斯科或格鲁吉亚，现实社会主义往往与奢华和新古典主义交织在一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些地方迷人的精髓", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此类图集通常的做法不同，阿马巴利（Amabali）和埃登显然没有依赖档案材料，而是亲自造访了所有介绍的地点。埃莱娜·安巴利（Elena Ambalis）的摄影既不是冷酷的建筑视角，也不是纯粹的怀旧；它们在氛围上高度凝练，仅通过几个视角就传达出其拍摄对象迷人的精髓。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡罗琳·埃登为此记下了与各个地点紧密相连的回忆：例如她第一次遇到deschurnaja（苏联时期监视客人的女看管员）的情景。2009年，“楼层女服务员”已经成为一个被束之高阁的过去的濒危遗迹。但在塔吉克斯坦首都杜尚别的瓦赫什酒店（Hotel Vakhsh），她们显然依然是活生生的热情好客的体现——或者有时恰好相反。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这本书最壮观的地方在于作者与摄影师双人组所呈现的那种惊人的同时性：世界上某些地方显然至今仍然是这副模样。乌兹别克斯坦塔什干酒店（Hotel Tashkent）走廊里装饰的室内植物，今天或许依然摆在那里。就好像这里刚刚拍完一部法斯宾德（Fasbinder）电影。德涅斯特河沿岸普雷特尼亚酒店（Hotel Pretenia）里的木质镶嵌工艺和让人联想到耶稣的青铜浮雕，其时代感大约就跟波兰卡托维兹酒店（Hotel Katowice）里那部带线的红色壁挂电话差不多。它们的建造与设计旨在追求永恒，但这种永恒从未兑现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如今还有谁想住在这样的酒店里？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种逝去的当下的记录还能持续多久，目前尚无定论。因为，正当西方至少有一小群人渴望兑现某种模糊的“东德怀旧”（Ostalgie）时，如今即使在地理上的东方，理所当然地，当前时兴的暴发户与斯堪的纳维亚风格（Skandi-Style）也比现实社会主义到共产主义时期的酒店建筑更受青睐。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿马比利和埃登共同造访的许多壮观建筑目前都处于失修状态。许多地方的“楼层女服务员”已经消失。在那些仍然营业的地方，过夜的客人也寥寥无几。作者诘问，如今还有谁想住在这样的酒店里？也就是那些将舒适视为被高估的属性、不仅闻起来霉湿陈旧、有时甚至还得自己带浴缸塞的地方？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种自主责任是否足以维持这些奇妙的时间胶囊，尚存疑问。但人们其实很容易想象出当今的目标受众：那些对设计或建筑充满热情、对世界任何精品酒店都找不到的那种审美约束力有着无限渴望的人。或者，干脆就是一个依然能够抵御短命世界精神的场所。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Zwischen Eleganz und Begrenzung: Ein neuer Bildband zeigt sozialistische Hotelarchitektur aus dem ehemaligen Ostblock. Die Fotos zeugen von einer ästhetischen Verbindlichkeit, die heute rar geworden ist

In der "Anything-goes-Post-Metamoderne" und einem Spätkapitalismus, der es global recht weit gebracht hat (ohne damit automatisch die freiheitlichen Vorzüge mitzubringen, die er mal versprochen hat), ist die Sehnsucht nach verbindlicher Ästhetik groß. Elena Amabili und Caroline Eden finden diese im Sozialismus. Genauer gesagt, in dessen Tourismusarchitekturen.

Die Serie "Socialist Hotels" versammelt Beispiele von Abchasien bis Usbekistan und aus allen Ländern dazwischen: Georgien, Albanien, Lettland, Litauen, der Ukraine, Russland, Moldawien, Polen, Rumänien und Serbien. Auch die ehemalige Deutsche Demokratische Republik (DDR) ist mit einigen Beispielen vertreten; die dortigen Hotels sind allerdings längst verlassen. Aus der Auswahl entsteht eine ungeahnte Fülle, die jetzt in Buchform erscheint.

Es ist diese spezielle Mischung aus Begrenzung und weltläufiger Eleganz, die vielen der vorgestellten Gebäude bis heute eine große Anziehungskraft verleiht. Manche Panorama-Lobby könnte problemlos als Aushängeschild westlicher Midcentury-Moderne in den kalifornischen Bergen stehen. Andere ehemalige Bettenburgen sehen freilich weniger generös aus, und in Moskau oder Georgien vermischt sich realer Sozialismus eher mit Prunk und Neoklassizismus.

Eine anziehende Essenz der Orte

Amabali und Eden verlassen sich offenbar nicht, wie sonst für Bildbände dieses Formats üblich, auf Archivmaterial, sondern haben alle vorgestellten Orte selbst aufgesucht. Elena Ambalis Fotografien sind weder kühle Architekturansichten noch reine Nostalgie; atmosphärisch verdichtet transportieren sie in wenigen Ansichten eine anziehende Essenz ihres Gegenstands.

Caroline Eden schreibt dazu Erinnerungen auf, die an die einzelnen Orte geknüpft sind: ihre erste Begegnung mit einer deschurnaja zum Beispiel, einer Aufseherin, die zu Sowjetzeiten über die Gäste wachte. 2009 waren die "Flurdamen" bereits ein vom Aussterben bedrohtes Relikt einer ad acta gelegten Vergangenheit. Doch im Hotel Vakhsh in Tadschikistans Hauptstadt Duschanbe waren sie offenbar noch lebendige Gastlichkeit – oder manchmal eben auch deren Gegenteil.

Das Spektakuläre an diesem Buch liegt in der erstaunlichen Gleichzeitigkeit, die das Autorin-Fotografin-Duo anbietet: Genau so sieht es offenbar noch immer in Teilen dieser Welt aus. Die Zimmerpflanzen, die die Flure im Hotel Tashkent in Usbekistan zieren, stehen dort womöglich noch heute. Als sei hier gerade erst ein Fassbinder-Film gedreht worden. Die Holzintarsien und an Jesus erinnernden Bronzereliefs im Hotel Pretenia in Transnistrien sind ungefähr so aktuell wie das rote Wandtelefon mit Schnur im Hotel Katowice in Polen. Gebaut und gestaltet für eine Ewigkeit, die so nie eingelöst wurde.

Wer will heute noch in solchen Hotels wohnen?

Wie lange diese Art der vergangenen Gegenwart noch dokumentiert werden kann, ist offen. Denn während sich zumindest eine kleine Gemeinde im Westen nach Einlösung einer diffusen Ostalgie sehnt, wird heute selbstverständlich auch im geografischen Osten die derzeit angesagte Mischung aus Nouveau Riche und Skandi-Style dem realsozialistischen bis kommunistischen Hotelbau vorgezogen.

Viele der spektakulären Gebäude, die Amabili und Eden gemeinsam besucht haben, befinden sich im Verfall. Die "Flurdamen" sind vielerorts verschwunden. Übernachtungsgäste werden, wo man noch geöffnet hat, rar. Wer, fragt die Autorin, wolle heute noch in solchen Hotels wohnen? Also dort, wo Komfort als überbewertet betrachtet wird und es nicht nur modrig-staubig riecht, sondern man bisweilen auch seinen eigenen Badewannenstöpsel mitbringen muss?

Ob solche Eigenverantwortung für einen Erhalt der fantastischen Zeitkapseln genügt, ist fraglich. Aber man kann sich eigentlich gut eine heutige Zielgruppe vorstellen: Design- oder Architekturaffine mit einem unbändigen Hunger nach ebenjener gestalterischen Verbindlichkeit, die man in keinem Boutiquehotel der Welt findet. Oder schlicht nach einem Ort, der dem kurzlebigen Weltgeist noch zu trotzen weiß.

article_text:
Owen Thiele hasn’t been on dating apps recently.

For good reason.

He and his boyfriend, celebrity stylist Jared Ellner, have been together for 10 years.

But that doesn’t mean he can’t help friends find love. Thiele stars in a new ad campaign for Tinder ’s Group Hangouts, which lets groups of friends meet other groups.

Related Stories

Netflix's ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee on Why Playing It Safe Is the Real Risk

Netflix, ‘Elite’ Star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll Adapt ‘La Regenta,’ a ‘Fresh Female Perspective’ on a Big Spanish Classic (EXCLUSIVE)

In the spot, from twin sister directors Fa and Fon Watkins in partnership with Vice Media’s Virtue Worldwide and Pulse Films, Thiele channels Sir David Attenborough as he observes and narrates Gen Z dating “in the wild” and what happens when they start meeting people via Group Hangouts.

It’s a full circle moment for Thiele and Ellner. “I’ve never told anyone this, but when Jared and I were dating for just a few months, a Tinder representative asked us to do a campaign for them,” Thiele says. “It was so strange. It was literally like three months into dating.”

They sat for a photo shoot. However, Thiele recalls, “Our faces were cut out and it was just our hands interlocked. So our hands are somewhere on a Tinder ad.”

I caught up with Thiele recently for an exclusive chat about Tinder, Anton and Paul Baker’s future on “ Adults ,” the “13 Going on 30” sequel and working with Connor Storrie in Molly Gordon’s A24 comedy “Peaked.”

You’ve had a boyfriend for 10 years, so when was the last time you were in the dating pool?

I haven’t been in the dating room for a second, but all of my friends, most of my friends, are single. I’m constantly trying to help them. I’m constantly matchmaking. But it never goes well. I shouldn’t be in charge of that. That shouldn’t be something that I’m in charge of. Luckily, there’s an app now where they can do it for you.

Have you had any success setting friends up?

Actually, yes. A friend of mine is dating another friend of mine that I set up. They’ve been dating for eight years.

You’re doing a little Sir David Attenborough cosplay in the campaign.

I’ve been doing ads for Tinder on my podcast, and they’ve just been such a collaborative, great partner. And then they approached me with this ad, and these two beautiful twins, Fa and Fon, directed it. These gorgeous girls directed this and came up with this fun idea where I was bird-watching, but it was actually people-watching. I was like, that sounds like something I would do. I would sit in a park and watch people all day if I could, and just read them. I signed on immediately.

But you didn’t do a British accent.

I didn’t do a British accent, which is honestly the best, I think Tinder would have taken a fall of some kind. Stocks would have been down if I had done that.

Anton and Paul Baker kiss at the end Season 2 of “Adults.” A third season hasn’t been greenlit yet, but if it does, do you think Anton and Paul Baker will be together?

Oh my God, I don’t know. Honestly, the writers have not told us anything, and they do this on purpose because of things like this. If they had told me, I would have said, “Marc, they’re going to be together. They’re getting married officially.” I think Paul Baker and Anton have found a really beautiful way to communicate that feels very honest and open and real. But I’m wondering what that would be like if they were actually in a relationship. I think right now it’s easy for them to communicate because they have this kind of will-they or won’t-they tension that’s building. But once that’s gone, what will happen? Anton’s crazy. Anton yells a lot. He’s constantly screaming. So I don’t know. I don’t know.

You’re also in the “13 Going on 30” sequel. Are you nervous about trying to live up to the original?

Yes, it is a sequel, but it’s a new thing. I don’t think it in any way does it try to be this iconic film that we all know and love. I feel very lucky to be a part of the lineage, I love “13 Going on 30.”

What was it like when Jennifer Garner walked on set ? That must have been surreal.

I wasn’t there because I had left for the day already. This is what happened: I get in my car, and I’m driving away as I see a black Escalade, and I was like, “Turn around, Owen, turn around, turn around.” I tried to turn around, but the security guard was like, “There’s no more spots on the lot.” I’m like, “No!”

You also have “Peaked,” directed by your childhood friend Molly Gordon.

She’s been directing me since we were two years old when we were in a play together, “Beauty and the Beast.” We were two years old at the Adderley School, and I’m not kidding. She’s one year older than me. I have memories of her telling me where to stand.

And your podcast guest Connor Storrie is in it. Did you get to work with him, or were you driving off the lot that day too?

I got to stay for that one. We have a few scenes together. He’s so brilliant. In every single interview, I somehow accidentally, but also on purpose, bring up Connor Storrie. There’s now this tally on Twitter that’s going around that I just saw recently, which is how many times can Owen Thiele bring up Connor Storrie? I read it being like, “This has to be fake.” But there’s proof for every single mention. I bring him up every time I can.

What is it like now working with him after the crazy success of “Heated Rivalry?”

He’s genuinely so humble and so down to earth and so wonderful and deeply cared about making Molly happy. He’s so collaborative. In one scene, I have like one line and he was like, “Am I giving you what you need?” I was like, “For my one line? Yes.” He cares so deeply. He’s genuinely a very well-trained actor. I come from an improv background where we’re constantly cutting each other off. I learned from him on set.

Watch Thiele’s Tinder video below.

article_text:
After her JFK airport arrest for alleged assault earlier this month, Selma Blair has broken her silence.

On Friday, the actress apologized in a statement as she explained that she never “intended to hurt or frighten anyone” when she allegedly tried to open an airplane door mid-flight to New York City and later assaulted airline employees.

“Hi, it’s me. I know I’ve been quiet for a couple of weeks since October 11, and you deserve to hear from me directly, and I’m sorry that it’s taken this long,” she prefaced in a video on Instagram. “There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I’m listening to them. And I take this very seriously.

Related Stories

Selma Blair Charged With Assaults On Cop & Nurse After Airplane Incident

Selma Blair Announces ‘Hineni’ Doc About Antisemitism After She Was “Erased” Over Islamophobic Comments

“What I can tell you though, is very simple and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life. And so, to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed, I am so sorry. And to the people that have written or called or sent wishes of love or caring, it has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as is Scout, who is also OK.”

Watch on Deadline

Blair continued, “So, right now, I’m going to be taking care of my health and my son, and thinking of you all with gratitude and love.”

On Sunday, Oct. 11, New York Port Authority police apprehended Blair after a flight from LAX, on which she allegedly tried to open the exit door mid-flight, before punching one airline employee and hitting another. Blair was also accused of hitting a cop at the airport and later a nurse at the hospital where she was transported.

Blair pleaded not guilty to two charges of second-degree assault for the latter two, and she was released on an $80,000 bond before she’s expected back in court on Jan. 19, 2027.

title_original: Alex Gibney on How a CGI Avatar Helped Simulate the Elon Musk Interview He Could Never Get
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Artificial intelligence serves as both a creative choice and a cautionary tale in Alex Gibney ‘s definitive nonfiction Elon Musk portrait, “ Musk ,” which is currently playing well in theaters — especially for a four-hour documentary about an uber-wealthy tech bro audiences are likely trying not to think about these days.", "links": [{"text": "Alex Gibney", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/alex-gibney/"}, {"text": "Musk", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/musk/"}, {"text": "Musk", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/musk-documentary-review-alex-gibney-elon-musk-1235215433/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Oscar-winning documentary filmmaker (“Taxi to the Dark Side”) joined IndieWire’s “ Screen Talk ” podcast this week for a wide-ranging chat with co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio. He talks about how his sole contact with the billionaire entrepreneur was over the X platform that Musk also runs. The brief exchange happened when Gibney first announced the project, and it also solidified how Gibney and his Jigsaw production team could absolutely never have secured a sit-down interview with the SpaceX and Tesla founder.", "links": [{"text": "Screen Talk", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/screen-talk/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/RP_B1327_b85318.jpg?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "Rachel Shane, Ayo Kepher-Maat, Julien Levesque, Erica Lee and Brent Lang at IndieWire Future of Filmmaking Summit held at Lumen on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/RP_B2706.jpg?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "Arash Ashtiani, Pegah Ahangarani and Brent Lang at IndieWire Art of the Doc 2026 held at Lumen on October 19, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "So the filmmakers had to get creative, using AI to construct an intentionally uncanny-valley avatar of Musk and to compile all his public remarks into a simulated “interview” with Gibney’s subject.", "links": [{"text": "AI", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/ai/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“We collected a massive database of stuff that Elon had actually said, and those recordings are the recordings that we actually use in the film ,” Gibney said. “We’re putting an avatar in the movie, but then playing these recordings. In addition to the archival clips of Musk, I wanted audio clips from podcasts and so on, but I also wanted to create the impression of an interview, which I thought would be interesting and important and fun. To visualize it … we took on board the idea of Musk’s own obsession with this idea that we’re living in a simulation, a kind of existential video game. So within that context, I thought, ‘OK, how about a simulated interview?’ This would then cinematically reflect on the larger themes of the film surrounding AI, our relationship with LLMs, and also his obsession with gaming and and simulations. And then we went to our wonderful design firm I’ve used on a number of films, including the Elizabeth Holmes film.”", "links": [{"text": "film", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/film/"}, {"text": "podcasts", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/podcasts/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Working with the integrated studio MakeMake, “we designed a set. We decided what clothes he would wear. We decided to put him in a gamer chair … [for his face] it’s a very flattering, if you ask me, portrait of Musk in terms of his sort of slender jaw and so forth and so on. Then, we used some AI tools to sync that figure to the audio, which is real audio.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "At the same time, “Musk” takes a cautionary position toward artificial intelligence’s capacities. As the documentary lays out, the Gen Z staff Musk appointed to his since-shuttered, ad hoc Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) accessed and archived a trove of U.S. citizen data while scaling back or jettisoning government agencies and programs. article_text:
Artificial intelligence serves as both a creative choice and a cautionary tale in Alex Gibney ‘s definitive nonfiction Elon Musk portrait, “ Musk ,” which is currently playing well in theaters — especially for a four-hour documentary about an uber-wealthy tech bro audiences are likely trying not to think about these days.

The Oscar-winning documentary filmmaker (“Taxi to the Dark Side”) joined IndieWire’s “ Screen Talk ” podcast this week for a wide-ranging chat with co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio. He talks about how his sole contact with the billionaire entrepreneur was over the X platform that Musk also runs. The brief exchange happened when Gibney first announced the project, and it also solidified how Gibney and his Jigsaw production team could absolutely never have secured a sit-down interview with the SpaceX and Tesla founder.

So the filmmakers had to get creative, using AI to construct an intentionally uncanny-valley avatar of Musk and to compile all his public remarks into a simulated “interview” with Gibney’s subject.

“We collected a massive database of stuff that Elon had actually said, and those recordings are the recordings that we actually use in the film ,” Gibney said. “We’re putting an avatar in the movie, but then playing these recordings. In addition to the archival clips of Musk, I wanted audio clips from podcasts and so on, but I also wanted to create the impression of an interview, which I thought would be interesting and important and fun. To visualize it … we took on board the idea of Musk’s own obsession with this idea that we’re living in a simulation, a kind of existential video game. So within that context, I thought, ‘OK, how about a simulated interview?’ This would then cinematically reflect on the larger themes of the film surrounding AI, our relationship with LLMs, and also his obsession with gaming and and simulations. And then we went to our wonderful design firm I’ve used on a number of films, including the Elizabeth Holmes film.”

Working with the integrated studio MakeMake, “we designed a set. We decided what clothes he would wear. We decided to put him in a gamer chair … [for his face] it’s a very flattering, if you ask me, portrait of Musk in terms of his sort of slender jaw and so forth and so on. Then, we used some AI tools to sync that figure to the audio, which is real audio.”

At the same time, “Musk” takes a cautionary position toward artificial intelligence’s capacities. As the documentary lays out, the Gen Z staff Musk appointed to his since-shuttered, ad hoc Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) accessed and archived a trove of U.S. citizen data while scaling back or jettisoning government agencies and programs. And that data could theoretically be used to manipulate the upcoming presidential election a la Facebook in 2020 .

“They have all our data that the federal government has. Now, was that transferred to SpaceX? We don’t know. We think it’s likely, and I think Geoffrey Hinton, who’s the godfather of AI, says, you know, if that happened, it would’ve been as easy as transferring a computer file into a folder,” Gibney said. “Then, you could train an AI with that data that would be enormously powerful in terms of doing stuff in the midterms, not just for the kind of Cambridge Analytica stuff that Zuckerberg did, or that was done via Facebook, but also through all sorts of plots and plans, like where do you devote your money? Let’s focus on questioning the citizenship of people with Latino names. All sorts of things are possible, but I think it was the idea of being able to train an AI on that private data on Americans that was troubling to Hinton, and that was Musk’s purpose, right?”

Listen to the episode below or on your preferred podcast platform.

article_text:
W hile people queue at the British Museum to see the Battle of Hastings , this excellent survey of LS Lowry at the MK Gallery in Milton Keynes takes you back to another, maybe more decisive part of our past – the age when Britain was the most industrialised society on Earth. Laurence Lowry was born in 1887 and worked for 41 years as a rent collector, a job that took him all over his native Greater Manchester observing its people and places. He had the city’s grime and grind in his soul. The MK wants to show him as a fully rounded artist, to uncover the Lowry with a song in his heart, but it’s the misery of his urban hell that holds and harrows you.

In his 1930 painting Coming from the Mill it’s the end of the shift and scores of people emerge from a factory’s bleak yellow gatehouse as if leaving prison. Their daily captivity has left them broken and exhausted and the little abstracted figures hunch forwards as they walk without pausing to laugh or chat, going to their separate homes, each one withdrawn, wretched. They are not the painting’s protagonists – they are passive victims. The architecture of industry dominates the picture as it rules their lives. How can any of these little people, dwarfed by the mill that eats their time and energy, attain individuality? No wonder they all look the same except for minor variations in their drab clothes. They’ve been reduced by the Industrial Revolution to matchstick people .

Lowry is the Franz Kafka of industrial Britain. He is not a naive artist who painted crudely because that’s the best he could do. Nor is he a patient social realist laying bare the injustices of capitalism – although Friedrich Engels would surely have recognised his Manchester. He is a modern expressionist who finds his inner melancholy reflected in the industrial sublime. He drinks in its despair, feasts on its poetry of alienation. As you journey through Lowry’s North, you sink ever further into his personal slough of despond.

Slough of Despond would make a good alternative title for his 1924 drawing The River Irwell at the Adelphi. Heaps of mud and ash choke the slow-moving river that runs through Salford, its shores lined with decaying sheds and slums against a smoggy, chimney-lined sky. It’s Lowry at his purest as he depicts the stunning, crushing presence of the city itself. He draws and paints the black, gnarled spires of urban churches with as much relish as those monstrous mills. In the second world war he was a fire-watcher with a privileged view of the blitz: a drawing of freshly bombed buildings in Piccadilly, Manchester shows husks of charred brick still wreathed in smoke.

This show digs out other, less well known dimensions to his talent. But his paintings of the Lake District are even more chilling than his cities. Lake Landscape, painted in 1950, is a vista of low curving hills divided by silvery still water, receding in abstract, musical pulses of sadness. No people or animals inhabit this eerie world. When he paints people close up it’s even more disturbing: a young man with staring eyes, a father and sons who all seem equally desperate. He lightens up to paint his ideal woman with a simplified doll-like face apparently intended as his tribute to Pre-Raphaelite red-lipped beauties but the result is weirdly robotic. Her face is on the exhibition merchandise, perhaps because Halloween is coming.

The most bizarre painting, however, is his 1963 work In a Park. At first glance it’s another city crowd scene until you realise everyone in this fenced enclosure has something different about them. A one-eyed face screams while people walk around the white-earthed, empty space with spinal deformities, facial palsies, amputated limbs. The catalogue gets itself in knots – is Lowry mocking the disabled or questioning how we define disability?

after newsletter promotion

But this painting is not about disability in a political sense at all. It uses it as an image of humanity in general: all people are broken and alone, misshapen in Lowry’s hopeless universe.

Lowry is a tricky customer. If it is pure snobbery to look down on him for being popular it is also patronising to see this troubled artist as a warmly sentimental nostalgist of the north. He is a painter of modern life in the age when that meant huge crowds staggering home in the shadow of smoking chimneys in cities blackened by carbon. At his best, Lowry is a great modern artist. His 1919 painting Pit Tragedy shows working-class people waiting for the worst news. They are statuesque, tragically posed in the grey dusty light. A woman turns towards us, her head veiled. Her pain is lost in the past but lives on here, observed and recorded by Lowry, visionary of the industrial age.

LS Lowry: The Theatre of Life is at MK Gallery, Milton Keynes until 28 February

article_text:
Nathan Fielder revealed in a new interview with Wired magazine that Elizabeth Holmes called him from prison right before the theatrical release of his new documentary, “ You Can See Everything .” The call marked the first time the director and his documentary subject had spoken in half a year. Ex-Theranos CEO Holmes is currently in federal prison after being convicted for fraud.

“She had not called me in over six months. I had not heard from her in any way… she asked how I was doing,” Fielder said about their conversation. “I asked her if she had seen any stuff about the film coming out and how she felt about it. She told me she had seen some stuff, but most things she just isn’t seeing, so she’s heard things, but she hasn’t really read anything. And then, at the end, she said to me – ‘I trust you.’ I said, ‘OK, thanks.’”

Related Stories

Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal

Fielder continued, “We talked about some other stuff. She talked about her kids, and then some updates that are not really my place to share. But then after that, she said again, at the end of the call— ‘I trust you.’ And I don’t know what she meant by that.”

Popular on Variety

“You Can See Everything,” directed by Fielder and “Primetime” helmer Lance Oppenheim, follows Holmes and her partner Billy Evans in their final weeks before Homes’ 11-year prison sentence begins. The filmmakers moved in with the couple 34 days before Holmes went to prison.

Fielder told Wired that he got involved with the project after hearing that Holmes and Evans had tried and failed to pitch a documentary about them to A24, explaining: “Months later, I heard that that had happened. So I called A24 and said, ‘Well, could I meet her?’ That was the start of it all.”

But why would Holmes allow Fielder to come into her home? That’s a question that still has Fielder puzzled considering his previous work, be it “Nathan for You” or “The Rehearsal,” should’ve made it clear to Holmes that bringing Fielder on board would not produce anything straightforward or conventional.

“This is part of the mystery that, like, doesn’t make sense to me,” Fielder said. “I asked her that on, I think, one of the first days we shot. I still don’t fully understand it. That really messed with my head. Also, I got the sense very early that she hadn’t seen a lot, but she had seen some of what I did, and she had talked to people who had seen what I did. Billy had seen more. I think she found the clip that she said she saw funny. But you know, her relationship to that … to what’s funny? I don’t even know. She said her favorite movie is ‘Elf,’ the Will Ferrell movie.”

Evans appeared on the “All-In” podcast the day before “You Can See Everything” opened in theaters and explained the couple’s rationale behind letting Fielder and Oppenheim into their home. Mainly, they wanted people to get to know Holmes up close and personal so they could decide for themselves if she is a bad person or not.

“It was to have people see who she is,” Evans said. “I have gone through this consistent experience with the people who love me most, from my grandmother to my best friends. They’d hear I knew [Elizabeth Holmes] or I was falling for this person and now we’re going to have a kid… in the beginning, every single one of these people thought I was crazy. ‘Do you know who she is?’ I would tell them, ‘I understand why you feel that way but just meet her.’ And they would meet her and spend time with her and see her in a totally natural environment, like going on a hike or helping a friend. Every opinion of her would radically shift. That was the intention of the film. To help scale that up and allow other people to sit with her and make up their own minds.”

The decision is backfiring for Holmes, however, since “You Can See Everything” is only amplifying the backlash against her. Even before the movie screened for press, A24 dropped a chilling teaser trailer that had many viewers disturbed by Holmes’ demeanor and claims that she did not do anything wrong at Theronos. The movie has since turned into a box office hit by grossing $15 million in its domestic debut, which is the biggest launch for a documentary in decades.

“You Can See Everything” is now playing in theaters nationwide. Head over to Wired’s website to read Fielder’s interview in its entirety.

在涵盖日式风情等多个备选方案中，我当时就觉得《城市之光》正是此选。至今为止，卓别林在全世界依然深受喜爱，海外观众也能乐在其中。不过，如果在6年前我刚就任艺术总监（2020年9月）的时候，这绝对是想都不敢想的剧目。剧中全都是对高难度技巧和自然演技有要求的角色，当时的演员阵容根本无法支撑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——也就是说，芭蕾舞团的演职员阵容变得如此雄厚了吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 我认为正是凭借目前团内的技术实力、演技，以及舞者们的主体性，才最终得以实现这部作品。不过，关于每位舞者如何进行自主思考这一点，依然还有很大的成长空间，这也是我希望进一步提升的部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/a6a7be09e3990ee4d6ce4790ce2d7ab6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "在《城市之光》中被提拔为主演的石山莲（右）等年轻一代的起用在演员阵容中十分引人注目。左为首席舞者柴山纱帆（于新国立剧场）", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "积极起用新人，用长远的眼光进行培养", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——最近的演员阵容安排也很大胆。主要角色对年轻一代的起用非常引人注目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 总之在年轻的时候，积累正式舞台的经验至关重要，因此哪怕存在一定风险，我也希望让他们去挑战。不过，为了避免承受过度的压力，我们在选角时也会注意平衡。每一次排练我们都会审慎观察到最后一刻再进行角色分配。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——在对新人的指导中，您最为注重的是什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 当以重要角色登上舞台时，无论谁都会满脑子想着“我想演这个”、“那个我也得做”，结果往往导致观众什么都没能感受到。我在年轻时也经常陷入这种模式。由于这是每个人都会经历的阶段，因此切忌贪多，首先要集中精力锁定一两个必须达成的要点并取得成果，这才是最重要的。作为指导者，往往会忍不住对各方面指手画脚，但我认为咬牙克制住这一点至关重要。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "营造让人对婚姻和生育充满希望的环境", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——说起芭蕾舞团最近的话题，进入产假和育儿假的舞者变得格外引人注目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 曾几何时，芭蕾界似乎有一种氛围，认为一旦生了孩子就必须离开舞团，因此选择生育大概需要相当大的觉悟。如今这种氛围已经有所淡化，大家在休完产假或育儿假后，已经能够以原先的职位回归舞团了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——这可以说是总监自上任之初就一直倡导的舞者周边环境建设工作的一部分吧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 每个人都是宝贵的战力，如果哪怕缺了一人，对运营而言确实并不轻松；但与此同时，将这里打造成为立志成为舞者的年轻人对结婚和生育充满希望的环境，也同样重要。如果不是处在稳定的环境中，大概也无法考虑这些选项吧，因此能够迈上这样一个台阶，我感到非常高兴。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/379b6060f23e718d29e76fed76c099ce.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "获得国际高度评价的《吉赛尔》伦敦公演（2025年7月） Photo by Tristram Kenton", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了瞄准“更高境界”，组织层面的课题堆积如山", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——距离获得世界高度评价的伦敦公演已经过去了1年，想必很多粉丝都在琢磨“接下来要去哪儿？”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 经历过皇家歌剧院的公演后，芭蕾舞团整体的实力毫无疑问得到了提升，这也让我重新深刻体会到了定期登上海外舞台的价值。然而，即便我们主观意愿极其强烈，要将其实现也绝非易事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——究竟是什么构成了阻碍？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 人数有限的工作人员在兼顾日常业务的同时，还要处理与海外的对接工作，这相当严峻。不仅如此，好不容易通过演出等途径与海外剧场相关人士建立起人脉、让交流变得顺畅之后，却往往因为定期的内部人事调动而导致负责人更换，经验无法积累，这样的情况并不少见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——这种人事轮岗，在新国立剧场这样的公共机构中似乎尤为常见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 我虽然也能理解人事轮岗的好处，但在我们这个世界里，彼此面熟的这种人际关系其实更为重要。我们不能仅仅依赖像我这样拥有海外经验的个人人脉，而是需要在作为组织传承人脉的同时加以拓展，完善知识积累的机制。剧场员工的职业发展与人事制度的应有形态等，有很多需要我们重新审视的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/21f443f59ec21004ab8734dfd5f482f6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "荣获英国舞蹈评论家协会奖“最佳舞团奖”。在颁奖仪式上微笑的艺术总监吉田都（右起第2人） Photo by Foteini Christofilopoulou", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样重视地方巡演", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——另一方面，在福冈和兵库举办的《吉赛尔》载誉归来公演因增设场次等原因，正汇聚着极高的人气。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉田 我们也将全国巡演视为新国立剧场芭蕾舞团的重要使命之一。因为有许多粉丝虽然很想看舞团的演出，却无法亲自赶到东京。我想在稳固国内根基、力争成为深受全国各位喜爱的芭蕾舞团的基础上，进而将之与海外拓展联系起来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "◇新国立剧场芭蕾舞团《城市之光》公开彩排 奥村康祐、米泽唯展示相遇等场景 以压倒性演技细腻映射心境 世界首演期待值高涨", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "◇专访新国立剧场芭蕾舞团首席舞者柴山纱帆 “积累经验后，演出的抽屉变丰富了” 新制作《城市之光》将打造成“喜剧元素丰富且充满深刻感动的作品”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "◇新国立剧场芭蕾舞团《城市之光》主演拔擢人选石山莲 “得知选角后食欲全无” “表现出温暖世界观的《城市之光》” “总监改变了我对待芭蕾态度的简单一句话”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
2026 ／ 2027 年シーズンの開幕を前に、新国立劇場の吉田都舞踊芸術監督にインタビューしました。芸術監督就任から６年を経過して近年のバレエ団の充実ぶりには自信を深め、テーマとしてきたダンサーを取り巻く環境整備も徐々に前進しているとした上で、日本を代表するバレエ団の一層の発展には劇場の組織や運営面の見直しも必要ではないかと指摘しました。（聞き手・「美術展ナビ」編集長 岡部匡志）

コメディとリアリズムが共存、魅力あふれる『街の灯』

―― シーズンの開幕を飾るのは新制作の『街の灯』です。チャップリンの不朽の名作を初めてバレエ化する、という世界的にも注目される取り組み。舞台の仕上がりはいかがでしょう。

吉田さん チャップリンの作品には、言葉に依らないパントマイム的表現や身体性、物語性が豊かに備わっていて、想像していた以上にバレエと高い親和性があると実感しながら進めているところです。

―― 原作をかなり忠実に再現しているそうですね。

吉田さん 有名なボクシングのシーンなども登場しますので、映画をご存じの方はぜひ楽しみにしていただきたいです。さらに振付のアラスター・マリオットさんのアイデアで、華やかでスペクタクルな要素を追加しました。ナイトクラブの場面では、スターダンサーが妙技を披露し、新国立劇場バレエ団ならではのコール・ド・バレエ（群舞）の見せ場があり、エンターテイメント性も豊富です。コメディ的な誇張と心に沁みるリアリズムが共存して、お客様の心に強く響く作品になると思います。また、チャップリンが作曲した音楽の使用をチャップリンオフィスに許可していただけたのも重要なポイントです。残念ながら宣伝では権利の関係で使用できないのですが、素晴らしい曲ばかりです。良い音楽があってこそのバレエなので。是非ご期待ください。

層が厚くなったバレエ団

―― 上演がますます楽しみになってきました。「街の灯」を新国立劇場バレエ団で、というのはマリオットさんの提案ですね。

吉田さん 和のテイストの提案などいくつかのプランがあった中で、「街の灯」こそこれだ、と思いました。今もなお、世界中でチャップリンは愛されていて、海外のお客様も楽しめますから。ですが、芸術監督に就任（ 2020 年 9 月）した当時の６年前だったら、挑戦することなど考えられない演目でした。難しいテクニックや自然な演技が求められる役ばかりで、キャスティングが成り立たなかったでしょう。

―― それだけ、バレエ団の層が厚くなった、ということでしょうか。

吉田さん 現在のカンパニーの技術力や演技力、そしてダンサーの主体性があってこそ実現できた作品だと思います。ただ、それぞれのダンサーが主体的に考える点はまだ伸びしろがあり、さらに高めていきたい部分ではありますが。

若手の起用、積極的に 長い目で育てる

―― 最近はキャスティングも大胆です。主要役に若手の起用が目立っています。

吉田さん とにかく若いうちは本番の舞台を経験することが大切なので、多少のリスクがあったとしてもチャレンジしてもらっています。ただし、過度のプレッシャーがかかることのないよう、バランスを取りながらのキャスティングです。ギリギリのタイミングまで見極めて配役しています。

―― 若手の指導で心がけていることは何でしょう。

吉田さん 大きな役で舞台に立つと、誰もが「あれをやりたい」「これもやらねば」という気持ちばかりが先走って、結果としてお客さまには何も伝わっていない、ということが起こりがちです。私も若手の頃はよくそのパターンに陥りました。誰もが通る道なので、欲張らず、まずは一つ、二つ、と達成するべきポイントを絞って結果を出すことが重要です。指導する側もあれこれ口を出したくなるものですが、そこをぐっと我慢するのが肝要だと思います。

結婚や出産に希望が持てる環境づくり

―― バレエ団の最近の話題といえば、産休や育休に入るダンサーさんが目立ちました。

吉田さん ひと昔前のバレエ界には、子どもができたらカンパニーを辞めなければならない、というような空気もあり、出産という選択は相当の覚悟が必要だったと思います。現在はそのような空気は薄れ、産休や育休明けには以前のポジションで戻ってくることができるようになりました。

―― 監督が就任当初から掲げてきたダンサーを取り巻く環境整備の一環ということですね。

吉田さん ひとりひとりが貴重な戦力なので、一人でも欠けてしまうと運営としては楽ではないのは確かですが、ダンサーを目指す方が結婚や出産に希望を持てる環境にすることも重要です。安定した環境でないとそういった選択肢も考えられないでしょうから、ひとつステップアップすることができて嬉しく思います。

「より上」を目指すには組織面の課題が山積

―― 世界的に高く評価されたロンドン公演から１年が過ぎ、「次はどこに？」と思うファンも多いと思います。

吉田さん ロイヤルオペラハウスの公演を経験して、間違いなくバレエ団全体の力が上がりましたので、定期的に海外の舞台を踏むことの価値を改めて感じました。しかしながら私たちにその気が十分にあっても、実現することは簡単ではありません。

―― 障壁になっているのは何でしょう。

吉田さん 限られた人数のスタッフが通常業務と並行して海外とのやり取りをこなすのはかなり厳しいのです。加えて、公演などを通じて海外の劇場関係者らとコネクションができ、話がスムーズに進むようになったと思ったら、定期的な人事異動で担当者が変わってしまったりして、経験が積み上がらないということが珍しくありません。

―― そのような人事ローテーションは、新国立劇場のような公的機関では特にありがちなことですね。

吉田さん 人事ローテーションのメリットも理解できるのですが、この世界では顔を互いに知っている、という関係のほうがむしろ大切だと思います。海外経験のある私のような個人のコネクションに依存するのではなく、組織として人脈を継承しつつ拡張し、知識蓄積の仕組みを整える必要があります。劇場スタッフのキャリア形成や人事のあり方など、見直したい点はたくさんあります。

地方公演も重視

―― 一方、福岡と兵庫で行われる「ジゼル」の凱旋公演は追加日程が入るなど、人気を集めています 。

吉田さん 全国公演も新国立劇場バレエ団にとって重要な使命のひとつと考えています。バレエ団の公演を見たいと思っていても、東京まで足を運べないファンの方がたくさんいらっしゃいますから。国内の足場を固めて、全国の皆様に愛されるバレエ団を目指すその先に、海外展開へ繋がればと思っています。

◇新国立劇場バレエ団「街の灯」で公開リハーサル 奥村康祐さん、米沢唯さんが出会いの場面など披露 心情を細やかに写す圧巻の演技 世界初演に高まる期待

◇新国立劇場バレエ団 プリンシパルの柴山紗帆さんに聞く 「経験を積み、演技の引き出しが増えた」 新制作「街の灯」は「コメディ要素豊富で、かつ深い感動のある作品に」

◇新国立劇場バレエ団「街の灯」で主役に抜擢の石山蓮さん 「キャスティングを知り、食事がのどを通らず」「心の温まる世界観が表現される『街の灯』」「バレエへの向き合い方を変えてくれた監督のひとこと」

article_text:
Book Review

Beverly Buchanan at the Raw Edge of Art

Instead of leaving the South behind, the polymath artist carried it into her writings, zines, paintings, and “shack sculptures” that echo the architecture of her childhood.

Beverly Buchanan was mentored by Norman Lewis and Romare Bearden, a contemporary of Ana Mendieta and Eva Hesse, and most recently featured in the 61st Venice Biennale in Koyo Kouoh’s In Minor Keys . Yet, the late artist and her oeuvre have long been understudied and underexplored.

With contributors ranging from friends, dealers, historians, curators, and contemporaries, Beverly Buchanan: Ruination and Regeneration (2026) seeks to amend this oversight. Above all, it is a testament to the North Carolina-born artist’s complexity, intellect, and sensitivity across sculpture, photography, land art, and video work. It’s also a reminder that the combined effects of racism and anti-Blackness, misogyny, and regional bias on an artist’s legacy must be counteracted, as modeled by the 18 contributors' voices in this book.

Edited by Aurélie Bernard Wortsman, the monograph begins with an introduction by Andrew Edlin, longtime dealer and supporter of the artist’s work. The essays, interviews, poems (including one by Alice Walker), and images within span Buchanan’s role in Abstract Expressionism and Post-minimalism; her activity in Atlanta, Macon, and Athens, Georgia; and her eventual departure to Michigan. An extensive selection of works is included: early paintings, zines, sketches, architectural and floral works on paper, environmental installations, and sculptures.

article_text:
The Baltic Event Co-Production Market has revealed its 15 projects to be pitched Nov. 18-20 at Tallinn’s Black Nights Film Festival industry sidebar Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event.

Picked out of 110 submissions from 34 countries, the slate of pics in development looking for co-financing, distribution and sales spans 10 territories – Finland, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Ukraine, Poland, Slovakia and Spain.

Related Stories

‘I Play Rocky’ Star Stephan James on Paying Tribute to Carl Weathers with His Red Carpet Look: ‘I Can Literally Walk in His Shoes Yet Again’

Julia Stiles Is 'Crying' at 'DWTS' Rehearsals Ahead of Heath Ledger Tribute: 'Bringing Back So Many Memories'

Leading the charge are “La Korena” by Basque helmer Joana Moya, produced by Sirimiri Films, founded by Estibaliz Urresola , director of the Berlinale winner “ 20,000 Species of Bees ,” and the horror satire “Wild Love” helmed by Lithuanian Jonas Trukanas (“Pensive”) for high profile prodco Afterschool , behind the 2021 Venice Horizons winner “Pilgrims” and 2024 Locarno winner “ Drowning Dry .”

Other buzzy projects taking in the Ukrainian-German-Czech “ Family Squad ” from Ukraine’s largest animation studio Animagrad , credited for the hit “Mavka: The Forest Song”, and the Latvia-French-Polish coming-of age “In the Truth by Tomas Harjo, produced by pedigreed Latvian outfit VFS Films (“The Rossellinis,” “Immortal”).

“ La Koreana ” forms part of a spotlight on the Basque region from the Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF), while a dominating Baltic crop (6 out of 15 titles) is aimed at boost the region’s top talent and co-production opportunities of other attendees with one of Spain’s most vibrant production hubs over the last five years.

For the Baltic Event Co-Production Market’s co-managers Helen Räim and Kärt Väinola, focusing on the Baltics was “very natural” as PÖFF turns 30, the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event is 25, and after the Oscar for “Flow,” the momentum on Baltic films shows no sign of waning. Not only was the Latvian doc “Ulya” selected at this year’s Cannes Film Festival (at Un Certain Regard), but so was “Vesna,” a co-production between Lithuania, France, Ukraine and Estonia, which was pitched at last year’s Baltic Event Co-Production Market and landed at Cannes’ Special Screenings.

Quizzed about common threads at this year’s lineup, Räin and Väinola cited belonging, love and growing up as “the strongest collective themes. “Heavier themes such violence, war and death also appear,” they said, “although often as secondary threads, approached through humor, satire and the search for oneself.”

“This year’s lineup shows filmmakers who are not afraid to face their own questions, doubts and worries about the world they live in and to dream of the world they hope for,” they added. The co-honchos also highlighted the substantial number of feature debuts (eight), often backed by “producers with strong track records at Venice, Berlin and Locarno,” and the strong slate of “imaginative stories for children and families, bringing fantasy and animation to the market.”

The 15 projects vying for the €20,000 ($22,300) Eurimages Co-Production Development Award will be judged by a panel of industry professionals including Eurimages’ Stefan Prohorov, Holly Daniel, director of the Red Sea Souk, and heavyweight Estonian producer Ivo Felt of Allfilm (“Tangerines,” “The Fencer”). A closer look at the Baltic Event Co-Production Market lineup:

“At Your Service” (Til þjónustu reiðubúinn,” Magnús Jónsson, Iceland, Estonia)

A dark comedy about a terminally ill artist who starts a euthanasia business after Iceland closes its nursing homes. From Icelandic producers Guðný Guðjónsdóttir and Sara Djeddou Baldursdóttir, also selected at Tallinn’s TV Beats showcase with the series “Kalmann.” The co-production with Estonia’s Munchhausen Films is backed by the Icelandic Film Centre, RÚV and Sambíóin.

“The Boy Who Loves the World” (“De jongen die van de wereld hield,” Steven Wouterlood , The Netherlands)

From the multi-awarded Dutch helmer of “ My Extraordinary Summer with Tess ,” and Int’l Emmy Kids winner “Anything Goes.” “Adapted from one of the most celebrated Dutch children’s books of recent years, [‘De jongen die van de wereld hield’], it’s an adventurous family film that dares to reflect on a polarized world, while leaving audiences with a deep sense of wonder and zest for life,” says Maiike Neve who produces with Joram Willink for Bind.

“Clusterfuck” (Läppä oli,” Juho-Pekka Tanskanen, Finland)

It’s a portrait of “youth and violence and how easily things can go sideways,” says producer Paria Eskandari of Danish Bear Productions. “At a time when young people are portrayed as dangerous or lost, the film explores how the lines between belonging, having fun and bullying can become blurred.” Co-produced with Finland’s Mohzi Films.

“Family Squad” (“Наша Файта,” Kostiantyn Fedorov, Ukraine, Germany, Czech Republic)

Pitched earlier at Cartoon Movie and Stuttgart’s Animation Production Days. Next feature from Animagrad and producer Anna Eliseeva, the team behind the animated hit “Mavka: The Forest Song,” which was released in 149 countries and grossed more than $25 million worldwide. Comedy drama in which a loser who dies by accident, is given a second chance in life, and sets off on a journey of self-discovery. Co-produced by Germany’s Telescope Animation and PFX, Czech Republic.

“Hide and Seek” (“Paslēpes,” Dace Puce, Latvia, Estonia, Sweden)

From the helmer of “The Pit,” Lübeck-Nordic Film Days top winner 2020, produced by Munchhausen Films, one of the Baltics leading servicing outlets. Thriller in which a Latvian mother’s life in Sweden unravels after she is accused of abusing her young daughter. “The project addresses themes that extend beyond Latvia: migration, belonging, adaptation, parental responsibility, children’s rights, and the challenges of navigating unfamiliar legal and social systems,” say producer Elīna Jozauska.

“In the Truth” (“Patiesībā,” Toms Harjo, Latvia)

Deeply personal pic from photographer, actor-turned filmmaker Toms Harjo, about his experience of growing up in a Jehovah Witness community. Produced by Latvia’s prominent doc and fiction outlet VFS Films, credited for “The Rossellinis,” Venice Critics Week closing film in 2020 and “Immortal,” best doc at Karlovy Vary 2019. “The Informatics Olympiad” (“Informatikos olimpiada,” Adas Burksaitis, Lithuania)

Estranged for years from his family, Domas has to take over his father’s job at school and prepare his niece for the informatics Olympiad. “Rooted in the specific world of provincial Lithuania and post-Soviet education, the film speaks universally about loneliness, addiction, burnout and the struggle to move beyond the identity imposed on us by others,” says Greta Akcijonaite from Magic Films.

“Lady Thatcher’s Feast” (“Uczta Pani Thatcher,” Marcin Kluczykowski, Poland)

From Polish prodco Telemark and producer Piotr Śmiechowski who won the Midpoint Series Award at last year’s TV Beats Forum in Tallinn for the comedy “We Are Still Here.” Set in 1996, we follow Maria, owner of a modest canteen, who is chosen to prepare a banquet for Margaret Thatcher. In this drama based on true events, “food is not simply part of the setting,” explains Śmiechowsk. “It becomes a way of expressing emotions, class differences, care, ambition and identity. The canteen itself becomes a microcosm of a society in transition.”

“La Koreana” (Joana Moya, Spain)

Feature debut from Basque director Joana Moya, produced by Sirimiri Films’ Estibaliz Urresola, director of the Berlinale winner “20,000 Species of Bees.” Set against a landscape shaped by iron mining, the film explores the relationship between nature, memory and human exploitation. Won the Ikusmira Berriak Prize at San Sebastian 2025.

“My 19-Year Old Granny” (“Moya 19-richna Babtsya,” Victoria Zadorska, Ukraine, Lithuania, Czech Republic)

Produced by Olena Yershova for Tato Film, in co-production with Lithuania’s Magic Films and the Czech Republic’s Breatless Films. Debut feature by fantasy author Victoria Zadorska, in which a retro dress teleports a schoolgirl to 1975 Soviet Ukraine, where she meets her hippie grandparents. “We want to connect three generations of women across two timelines and reveal what it truly costs to finally trust yourself,” says Yershova.

“My World Upside Down” (“Nikomu to nepoviem,” Daniel Rihák, Slovakia)

Feature debut by Rihák, whose short film “The Trip” was shortlisted for the BAFTA Student Film Awards. When Miško, a 12-year-old boy from a Slovakian village, discovers his brother is gay, he decides to save him “from hell.” But his plan backfires and Miško’s world turns upside down. Produced by What If Films.

“Shadows of Summer” (“Suve varjud,” Helen Takkin, Estonia)

“Shadows of Summer” tackles sensitive and deeply relevant issues of power dynamics, bullying, and co-dependency,” says producer Elisabeth Madisson of Nafta Films. “By intertwining a present-day participatory theater performance with events from 16 years earlier, the film gradually blurs the boundaries between past and present, reality and performance, bringing a fresh and distinctive cinematic approach to themes that are both universal and pressing today.”

“Summer of the Moth” (“Yöperhosen kesä,” Veera Lamminpää, Finland)

Produced by Petri Kemppinen of Good Hand Production. Story of a grumpy old elderly gardener and a magical time-traveling moth whose unexpected journey into the past helps them rediscover imagination, trust and hope. “Told through a rare mix of stop motion animation and live action, the film combines an appealing sense of humor with layered storytelling,” says Kemppinen.

“Wild Love” (“Laukine Meile,” Jonas Trukanas, Lithuania, Estonia)

From rising genre talent Trukanas whose breakthrough pic “Pensive” was bought by Cinedigm for their specialized platform Screambox. Produced by Afterschool, behind Lithuania’s Oscar hopefuls “Pilgrims,” and “Drowning Dry.” Co-produced by Estonia’s Tallifornia. “’Wild Love’ is a rare Baltic horror satire,” say producers Klementina Remeikaitė and Rūta Kiaupaitė. “Set on Saaremaa Island, it plays on the nostalgia for Robinsons, the 2000s reality hit that whole Baltic families watched, and sends it spiraling into a zombie outbreak, in which the reality show at the heart of the film reflects a world where our sense of what is real keeps shifting and truth slips into lies.” “Zona” (“Samosioły,” Bartosz Brzeziński, Poland, Lithuania, Estonia)

Directorial debut produced by Zizu Films. Intimate drama set in the Chernobyl exclusion zone, where a young Ukrainian deserter finds refuge with an elderly woman and forms an unlikely bond. “War trauma is explored through a fresh lens, combining an intimate character study with the haunting backdrop of the Chernobyl wilderness,” says Klaudia Pachuta who produces with Konrad Zagórski, and Karol Zagórski.

article_text:
Mexico’s Santiago Maza, whose fourth feature-length doc “State of Silence,” (“Estado de Silencio”), a passion project of Diego Luna, snagged the best feature award at Chile’s 2024 Santiago Film Festival (Sanfic), has premiered his latest work, “Black Shine” (“El brillo negro”) at the Morelia Film Festival where it competes for the top prize among the multiple short films in competition.

Set in Coahuila’s coal-mining region in Mexico, “Black Shine” revisits the 2006 Pasta de Conchos mine explosion that buried 65 miners. Two decades later, after years of neglect and impunity, families continue their fight for the recovery of their loved ones.

Related Stories

H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair

Ethan Klein Reacts to Hila Klein's Cheating Allegations Amid 'H3 Podcast' Fallout: 'Please Respect My Family's Privacy ... They Have Nothing to Do With This'

Like “State of Silence,” which centers on the high death count of reporters in Mexico through the lives of four journalists, “Black Shine” focuses on two people in particular: El Güero, a former miner who has recovered his brother’s remains, and Elvira, still waiting for her husband. The doc portrays grief as an enduring act of resistance and a refusal to let those lost beneath the earth be forgotten.

Speaking to Variety at Morelia, Maza relates how he met them in 2021 when he traveled to Coahuila to shoot a short film about climate change. There he met with the Pasta de Conchos organization which had been spearheading the fight to dig up the long-buried bodies, some of which have been recovered. “After 20 years of fighting for the recovery of the miners’ bodies, the families began experiencing deeply cathartic moments of rescue, like funerals filled with light and a long-awaited sense of peace.”

“The organization invited me to document this process and it felt right. I wanted to make a film that acknowledged the political weight of the struggle while focusing on its emotional dimension. Through the organization, I met Elvia and El Güero. Their stories felt like two sides of the same journey toward closure, capturing the possibility of peace after two decades of struggle.”

He adds: “When the disaster happened in 2006, the mining company and the government effectively colluded to cover it up. They never properly searched for the miners. That was the second tragedy: the corruption and impunity that kept their families from recovering their loved ones. Three presidential administrations went by before the recovery began, backed by Andrés Manuel López Obrador, who had visited the site in 2006 and promised that, if elected president, he would make the recovery happen.”

Juxtaposed against the images of a blighted landscape, Coahuila-born writer, Julián Herbert, reads lines from a poem he wrote for the short: “It is the patience that endures, the water for the thirst of those who wait. Where there is love, there is no complete loss: there is the next sentence, the memory that stains and fades, the dawns that return. In the face of abandonment, presence: a fragile flash of lightning, light emanating from the act of waiting.”

“I think it adds another layer to the short film, allowing us to explore the symbolism behind the whole situation,” Maza notes.

Filmed in April with a four-person crew and minimal pre-production, “Black Shine” emerged from an instinctive, flexible approach. “This time, I pushed myself to trust my instincts and the visuals.” Over four intense shooting days, the team moved freely across the region, capturing landscapes and details that reveal its history and its people. As longtime collaborators, their shared understanding allowed them to work intuitively and immerse themselves more deeply in the story, embracing the agility of a small crew to get closer to the people and places they filmed.

Maza is next plunging into a new format for him, the mockumentary. Based on a documentary filmmaker not unlike himself, “Ecocides, Repent!” (“Ecocidas ¡Arrepentíos!”) has some autobiographical elements in it, he admits.

The documentarian discovers a support group, somewhat like an Alcoholics Anonymous but for people who have harmed the environment. Some have polluted rivers, destroyed forests or contaminated cenotes [sinkholes], and all struggle with guilt. Using dark humor, the doc explores the lack of consequences for environmental damage in Mexico and around the world.

“He starts becoming the vehicle for them to work through their guilt, but in the end, he realizes that he also has his own regrets to work through.”

The script has been completed and the next step is seeking state support in Mexico.

“Ideally, I’d like to develop it as a co-production with Spain, since part of the story takes place there. We might shoot a small portion in Spain, but most of the film would be shot in Mexico. The country has such a diversity of ecosystems, from deserts to jungles and the environments affected by pollution in the story can all be found here. That’s what allows the character to travel and explore these different landscapes.”

The 24 th Morelia Film Festival wraps on Oct. 25.

article_text:
東京・パナソニック汐留美術館で10月15日、「吉田璋也のデザイン ― 新作民藝運動がめざした未来」が開幕します。 吉田 璋也 （1898‒1972）は 鳥取県で医師をしながら、 柳 宗悦 ら の提唱する「民藝」運動を支え、陶芸家の河井寬次郎からは「民藝の母」と評された人物です。新しい民藝のデザインから、プロダクトの生産・流通・販売の仕組みづくりまでこなしたマルチな活躍は、中国大陸にも及びました。内覧会ではそれらを余すところなく展示されていて、感服の一言でした。

吉田璋也のデザイン ― 新作民藝運動がめざした未来

会場：パナソニック汐留美術館（東京都港区東新橋1-5-1 パナソニック東京汐留ビル4階）

会期：2026年10月15日（木）～12月20日（日）

休館日：水曜休館。ただし12月16日は開館

開館時間：午前10時～午後6時（入館は午後5時30分まで） ※11月6日（金）・12月4日（金）・12月18日（金）・12月19日（土）は夜間開館 午後8時まで開館（入館は午後7時30分まで）

アクセス：ＪＲ新橋駅「汐留口」「銀座口」「汐留地下改札」より徒歩約８分、東京メトロ銀座線新橋駅「２番出口」より徒歩約６分、都営浅草線新橋駅「ＪＲ新橋駅・汐留方面改札」より徒歩約６分、ゆりかもめ新橋駅より徒歩約６分、都営大江戸線汐留駅「３・４番出口」より徒歩約５分

観覧料：一般：1200円、65歳以上：1100円、大学生・高校生：700円、中学生以下：無料 ※障がい者手帳またはミライロIDをご提示の方、および付添者1名まで無料でご入館いただけます。

※詳細情報は 美術館公式サイト で確認を

展示の最初に《緑釉黒釉染分皿》がありました。吉田の新作民藝の記念すべき最初のデザインに基づく皿で、鳥取民藝のアイコンとなっています。さらに特別展示として、「旧吉田医院」の診察室が再現されていました。1952年の鳥取大火で焼失した医院を、大工と一緒に再建した様子が、会場の展示動画で見られました。木製車輪のついた吉田愛用の椅子や、高さを調整できる患者用椅子など、興味深いデザインばかりです。

序章の展示は、吉田が蒐集した民藝作品のダイジェストです。洋の東西を問わず、「美の標準」となるような工芸品が凝縮されています。吉田は職人たちに具体的な手本となるような作品を意識して蒐集していたそうです。吉田は単に「昔のものは素晴らしい」というだけでなく、新しくデザインしていこうという前向きな意欲にあふれていました。

こちらの展示は実際に吉田の家族写真に写り込んでいた品々です。ぜひ会場で写真と展示品を見比べてみてください。

吉田は医学生として過ごした新潟で、『白樺』を愛読する仲間や、人生の師と仰ぐ柳宗悦に出会い、やがて民藝運動へと歩み始めます。郷里の鳥取の工芸品で出会った茶碗が、新作民藝運動の端緒となったと解説がありました。また、新作民藝のプロデュースや販売のことで、柳と書簡を交わしています。価格をどうするか、参考になるデザインはないか、様々な相談ごとが興味深く解説されていました。

吉田のプロデュースした工芸品は幅広い生活用品にわたっています。電気スタンドもペン立てもインク壺も栓抜きもネクタイも。電気スタンドは日本映画の巨匠小津安二郎監督も愛用し、映画の小道具に使われていたというエピソードは興味深いものです。

工芸品をセットにした展示も見どころです。今でも憧れる落ち着いた室内風景にはうっとりします。「機能性の美」を具体的に示してくれて、民藝の精神が浅学の身にも伝わってきました。

終盤に、吉田と交誼を結んだ芸術家たちの展示が集まっていました。大正から昭和中盤にかけての困難な時代を豊かに生きてきた先人たちに、尊敬の念を抱かずにおられません。吉田も戦時中は軍医として中国大陸に赴き、召集を解除されて以降も再び中国へ渡り、北京で新作民藝に取り組んでいたという前向きさに打たれました。

会場前のロビーで、13分の動画が流れています。吉田は「生まれ変わったら建築家になりたい」と話していたそうで、建築をめぐる吉田の物語が凝縮されていて、大変興味深いものでした。これも含めて、民藝をめぐる沢山のエピソードに満ちた展覧会です。「民藝」をテーマに同時開催している静嘉堂文庫美術館の「民藝SHOCK!! ー 没後60年静嘉堂の河井寬次郎」（11月8日まで）とは、相互割引を実施していますので、どちらかに行ったら半券を捨てずに両方楽しみましょう。（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班・丸山謙一）

article_text:
The Japan IP Market will be back in Cannes next May for a second straight year. The Cannes Film Market and TIFFCOM , the content market of the Tokyo International Film Festival , are again teaming up on the event, and the 2027 edition will run May 14-15.

The return was revealed at TIFFCOM in Tokyo, during a conference on how Japan can forge new international partnerships after its stint as Country of Honor in Cannes. Alexandra Zakharchenko, head of industry programs at the Cannes Film Market, was among the panelists.

Related Stories

CAA, WME and UTA Lead Coalition Pushing for Law to Force Streamers to Spend Half Their Content Budgets on Indie Productions

Agencies and Producers Back U.S. Tax Incentive as 'First Step' Toward Hollywood Recovery

“The success of Japan, Country of Honor showed what can happen when a focused national presence creates lasting opportunities for the industry. The Japan IP Market is one of those outcomes: a collaboration that extends beyond a single edition and gives Japanese intellectual properties greater access to international partners,” said Guillaume Esmiol, executive director of the Cannes Film Market. “I’m delighted that we are continuing this work with TIFFCOM to create more opportunities for rights holders to connect with international producers and partners, develop new adaptations and bring their stories to global audiences.”

The Japan IP Market first ran in May 2026, one of the initiatives tied to Japan’s turn as Country of Honor at the Cannes Film Market. It put Japanese rights holders in the same room as industry professionals from abroad via pitches, one-on-one meetings and industry discussions. Kadokawa, Shochiku and Toei Company were among the companies taking part. The speaker lineup included Fujimura Tetsu, executive producer of “One Piece” and founder and CEO of Filosophia, Inc.

“The Japan IP Market is about creating the right conditions for business opportunities between Japanese rights holders and international companies,” said Zakharchenko. “By bringing them together in Cannes, we can help turn growing interest in Japanese content into concrete adaptation deals and acquisitions, while fostering new collaboration opportunities.”

Shiina Yasushi, executive adviser at UNIJAPAN and CEO of TIFFCOM, said the partnership with the Cannes market plays an important role for Japan’s audiovisual industry. He described the Cannes market as the biggest market attached to any film festival in the world. “Meeting the international professionals who gather there and creating together with them is the key to nurturing Japanese IP into global content,” he said.

Ikeda Kaori, managing director of TIFFCOM, said the first edition had shown how keen producers and partners worldwide are on Japanese IP. “Through the continued partnership linking Cannes in May with the Tokyo IP Market in October, we are pleased to offer more professionals the opportunity to meet Japanese rights holders directly and discover the rich diversity of Japanese IP,” she said.

The 2027 roster of companies and the rest of the program will be unveiled in the months ahead.

ごじゃっぺタクシー

劇場公開日： 2026年10月17日

予告編を見る

解説・あらすじ

死に場所を求めて故郷・茨城に戻った男が、謎のタクシー運転手に導かれて過去に縁を持った女たちのもとを巡りながら、自らの人生と向き合っていく姿を描いたヒューマンドラマ。 東京で内縁の妻と息子と暮らす中村健人は、ある日突然、身に覚えのない借金を背負わされてしまう。家庭は崩壊し、追い詰められた中村は死に場所を求めて故郷・茨城に足を運ぶ。地元の神社で「楽に死ねますように」と願掛けした翌日、謎のタクシー運転手が姿を現し、中村の胸の内を詠む。彼が運転する“終活タクシー”に乗り込んだ中村は、過去に関係を持った女たちを巡る旅に出る。さまざまな再会を通して中村の無責任さや逃げ癖があぶり出されるなか、やがて彼はこのまま「死にたくない」という本音にぶつかっていく。 茨城県出身の同級生である俳優の岩田和浩と草野速仁がダブル主演を務めた。オガワセイイチが監督・脚本・編集、俳優の奥田瑛二が監修を担当。タイトルの「ごじゃっぺ」は茨城県で使用される方言で「でたらめ」を意味する。ゆうばり国際映画祭2026で観客賞を受賞。

article_text:
Everyone in Hollywood is always looking for the next big hit, but the process of actually finding one is a unique combination of art, science, and luck. There’s no one way to learn how to look for hits (or sell them to those who are searching for them), but listening to opinions from smart people at every step of the process is a great place to start.

At our Future of Filmmaking Summit in Los Angeles, a panel that included Erica Lee (president of production and partner, Thunder Road), Julien Levesque (agent, Gersh) Ayo Kepher-Maat (VP of acquisitions and productions, Independent Film Company), and Rachel Shane (head of film and television, Madison Wells) sat down with IndieWire editor-in-chief Brent Lang for a wide-ranging conversation about what it takes to find a breakout hit in 2026.

The discussion covered the actual art of in-person pitching, working with producers, the value of writing on spec, and even the next genre that might be poised for a comeback (spoiler: more than one panelist thinks it might be erotic thrillers). If you’re looking to build a film career at any stage of the process, the Pitch Me panel is a must-watch.

Check out the complete conversation in the video above.

IndieWire Future of Filmmaking 2026 Summit is presented by AT&T Untold Stories, an impactful multi-year collaboration between AT&T and Tribeca Festival that awards $1.2 million dollars, mentorship, and comprehensive support to the next generation of filmmakers looking to bring their films to the big screen. For more information, visit here .
excerpt_original: At IndieWire's Future of Filmmaking Summit, a panel of executives and representatives explain how they look for breakout hits.

title_original: Maria Kreyn’s New Paintings Fuse Science, Myth, and the Sublime
editorial_title_zh: 玛丽亚·克雷恩的新画作融合了科学、神话与崇高
editorial_excerpt_zh: 克雷恩的全新展览由 M.O.N. 艺术基金会策划，并与伦敦弗里兹艺博会同期举办，将祭坛化为一座关于创造、消解与重生的纪念碑。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在伦敦考文特花园的瑞士教堂内，艺术家玛丽亚·克雷恩精心打造了一个沉浸式世界，与这座历史悠久的 18 世纪帕拉迪奥式场馆自身的精神与心理主题遥相呼应。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "值此弗里兹周之际，由 M.O.N. 艺术基金会策划的“梦境逻辑”（“Dream Logic”）将展出至 10 月 19 日星期一。展览汇集了一系列全新的绘画作品，定格了翻滚、充满光线的风暴，其中犀利的几何形态划破了柔和的大气云层。在这座始建于 1855 年、后由建筑师伊曼纽尔·克里斯特（Emanuel Christ）和克里斯托夫·甘滕bein（Christoph Gantenbein）通过镜像屏风进行更新的教堂中，克雷恩的作品巧妙地呼应了新旧交织的层次感，将该处的建筑视为积极的合作者，而非中性的背景。", "links": [{"text": "M.O.N. Art Foundation", "url": "https://www.monartfoundation.com/"}, {"text": "Dream Logic", "url": "https://ministryofnomads.com/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/app/news-upload/2026/10/maria-kreyn-london-2026-1024x672.jpg", "alt": "玛丽亚·克雷恩在伦敦考文特花园瑞士教堂举办的展览“梦境逻辑”的装置现场，展示了教堂白色穹顶后殿内放置在金属支架上的三幅大型独立画作。位于中央的画作置于升高的高台上，描绘了一条金色的DNA双螺旋楼梯，两侧则是以戏剧性的蓝色、白色和炽热的橙色渲染的两幅大气风暴画作。", "caption": "", "credit": "Artnet News", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“玛丽亚·克雷恩：梦境逻辑”（2026年）装置现场。图片由 Ministry of Nomads 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克雷恩承袭了 J.M.W. 透纳等浪漫主义画家的传统，与前辈一样，这位美国艺术家对自然及其力量怀有敬畏，同时融入了更多数学和异世界的元素——给人一种在风暴的混乱之下，隐藏结构正在发挥作用的感觉。她的新展览尤其从莱昂诺拉·卡林顿（Leonora Carrington）和大卫·林奇（David Lynch）等超现实主义者那里汲取了更多灵感，这些艺术家深知如何通过作品传达梦境无边界、特立独行的逻辑。同样，克雷恩的画作也表达了一种替代性的秩序，这种秩序建立在直觉与联想之上，而非因果关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/app/news-upload/2026/10/maria-kreyn-a-palm-readers-manual-2026-682x1024.jpeg", "alt": "玛丽亚·克雷恩题为《手相师手册》（2026年）的画作，描绘了画布上方翻滚、发光的淡云和半透明几何形态风暴，下方则呈现出暖珊瑚色、橙色和金色调的湍流般的火焰状波浪。这一构图唤起了平静的大气光线与翻滚、炽热的海面之间戏剧性的过渡。", "caption": "", "credit": "Artnet News", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", article_text:
At the Swiss Church in Covent Garden, London, artist Maria Kreyn has crafted an immersive world that echoes the spiritual and psychological themes of the historic 18th-century Palladian-style venue itself.

Timed to Frieze Week and organized by the M.O.N. Art Foundation , “ Dream Logic ,” which runs through Monday, October 19, brings together a new body of paintings that capture swirling, light-filled storms, where sharp geometric forms cut through soft, atmospheric clouds. At the church—originally built in 1855 and later updated with a mirrored screen by architects Emanuel Christ and Christoph Gantenbein —Kreyn’s work plays off the layering of old and new, approaching the site’s architecture as an active collaborator rather than a neutral backdrop.

Installation view of “Maria Kreyn: Dream Logic” (2026). Courtesy ofCourtesy of Ministry of Nomads.

Kreyn operates in the tradition of such Romantic painters as J.M.W. Turner , and, like her forebears, the American shows a reverence for nature and its power, while layering in something more mathematical and otherworldly—a sense that beneath the chaos of the atmosphere, a hidden structure is at work. Her new show, in particular, takes further inspiration from surrealists like Leonora Carrington and David Lynch , artists who understood how to communicate the unbounded, idiosyncratic logic of dreams through their work. Kreyn’s paintings, likewise, express an alternate form of order, one built on intuition and association, rather than cause and effect.

Maria Kreyn, A Palm Reader’s Manual (2026). Courtesy of Ministry of Nomads.

Anchoring the exhibition is the monumental 2026 canvas The Alchemist’s Coil , which is installed at the altar in place of an expected religious centerpiece. Here, Kreyn renders a golden spiral staircase that doubles as a DNA helix, winding its way upward through a glowing landscape that evokes a type of alien inferno. The composition draws loosely on assembly theory, a scientific framework linking the origins of life to ideas about complexity and memory embedded in matter itself—fitting territory for an artist who studied mathematics and philosophy at the University of Chicago before teaching herself to paint.

Installation view of “Maria Kreyn: Dream Logic” (2026). Courtesy of

“Dream Logic” marks Kreyn’s third major presentation inside of a sacred space, following a pair of shows abroad. In 2024, her exhibition for the 60th Venice Biennale , “ Chronos ,” filled St. George’s Anglican Church with a suite of tempestuous seascapes that also built on the tradition of artists like Turner and Caspar David Friedrich , reflecting a shift in her practice away from the figure and toward pure atmosphere. And, last autumn, “ Hyperobject ” brought a new set of storm paintings to London’s Fitzrovia Chapel , anchored by an altarpiece built around the show’s titular concept of hyperobjects, phenomena too vast in scale for humans to comprehend or grasp fully.

All three shows were produced by the M.O.N. Art Foundation, helmed by curator and gallerist Maria Vega , who founded the organization’s parent gallery, Ministry of Nomads , in 2008. Vega has described her mission as pushing contemporary art outside of the conventional gallery model, pairing artists with culturally rich, unconventional spaces where dialogue between art, science, and belief can unfold. Her ongoing collaboration with Kreyn has become a true through line and exemplary of this mission.

Maria Kreyn, The Second Concerto (2026). Courtesy of Ministry of Nomads.

“ Maria Kreyn: Dream Logic ” is on view at the Swiss Church, Covent Garden, London, through October 19, 2026.

ビックリするほど当たるためIMA御用達の占い師・マコが、12星座の今をタロット1枚で運気予報！フォトグラファー清水はるみによるファンタスティックな星座＆大アルカナのヴィジュアルと共に、明るい未来の指針を毎月前・後半でお届けします。

10月後半に思うこと

「映画『ディスクロージャー・デイ』と、映画館で凡人占い師が覚醒し損ねた話」

10月後半、秋の夜長に楽しみたいのはやっぱり映画！SF大好きっ子の私、スティーヴン・スピルバーグ監督の最新作『ディスクロージャー・デイ』を観に行ってまいりました。観終わった率直な感想は……「うーん、スピルバーグ作品にしては意外と普通？こんなもん？思ってたんとちゃう」というのが正直なところ。ところが、帰宅後にSNSで感想を検索してみると、映画本編以上に刺激的な世界が広がっていたのです。

「劇中でなぜか涙が止まらなかった。ついに覚醒が始まったようだ」

「実は昔アブダクトされた経験があり、その時の恐怖を思い出して震えが止まらなかった」

「日本人を覚醒させないための罠が仕掛けられている映画なので注意して！」

「やっぱり私はただの主婦ではなかった、選ばれた人間。立ち上がります！」

「劇中の宇宙語がわかりました！実は宇宙語話せます」と宇宙語喋り出す動画……。

などなど、映画の何倍もドラマチックで香ばしい口コミが溢れかえっているではありませんか！

で、肝心の私はというと。劇中のクライマックスシーンの真っただ中で、猛烈な尿意に襲われる。涙どころか大惨事1歩手前。こんなシーンでど真ん中の席から離席などできるはずもなく、「あぁ宇宙人よ、どうか私をトイレにアブダクトしてくれたまえ。遣いの赤い鳥よカモーン｣と赤い鳥を召喚してみるが待ち人来ず。上映が終わった瞬間にトイレへダッシュすることしか考えられなくなっておりました。最後に宇宙人が耳打ちした言葉はきっと｢次からはボンタンアメ仕込んで来いよ｣でしょうか。

宇宙からのメッセージも覚醒の兆候も、すべて尿意によってかき消された私。どうやら見事に「凡人確定」のようです。

占いでも「周囲の熱狂に流されず、自分の身に起きたリアルな感覚や直感を信じること」が開運の基本とお伝えします。壮大な真実よりも、自分の感覚を大切に。

そんな凡人タロット占い師の私、秋の終わりの京都で皆様をお待ちしております！

【お知らせ】 11月29日（日）、京都・安井金比羅宮の近くの「cafe vegan terrace カフェ ヴィーガン テラス（ホテル祇園エリートテラス1階）」にて秋の占いイベントが開催されます。私はタロット占いで参加いたします！お時間がありましたら、ぜひ遊びにいらしてくださいね。詳細は私のInstagramをご確認ください！

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: When it comes to the PAW Patrol franchise, it’s been not a good dog but a great one at the box office. Add $18 billion in lifetime retail, and it only makes sense for Spin Master Corp, Paramount Animation and Nickelodeon Movies to team on a fourth, currently titled PAW Patrol 4. A 2029 theatrical release is being eyed via Paramount.

Related Stories

The 30 Highest-Grossing Animated Films Of All Time At The Global Box Office

The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

Cal Brunker, who helmed the previous films — PAW Patrol: The Movie, PAW Patrol: The Mighty Movie , PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie , which grossed more than a half-billion dollars worldwide — is back to direct and will co-write with Bob Barlen.

“ PAW Patrol is a global entertainment phenomenon, and we’re investing in the franchise to give fans more of what they love,” said Vishnu Athreya, EVP & President of Spin Master Entertainment. “Looking to the future, we want to further expand the PAW Patrol universe through movies, series, specials, short-form video and connected play to bring joy to the next generation of kids wherever they are. There are endless storytelling possibilities — this is just the beginning.”

Watch on Deadline

Said Jennifer Dodge, President of Paramount Animation: “ PAW Patrol has a special place in the hearts of families around the world, and we’re thrilled to continue the pups’ journey on the big screen. Together, with our partners at Spin Master, we’re excited to bring audiences another adventure that’s made for the theatrical experience.”

Dodge worked previously at Spin Master, building out its entertainment division.

“Watching the way audiences have connected with the PAW movies has been incredible,” said Brunker. “We’ve written a new story that we think audiences are going to love, and we can’t wait to share it with the world.”

PAW Patrol has ranked as the No. 1 preschool show on Nick Jr. since its 2013 debut. PAW Patrol ’s global reach spans over 190 territories and 33 languages, and it has amassed more than 10 million YouTube subscribers. The franchise also counts more than 1,000 licensees worldwide.

Skydance Products & Publishing handles the consumer products licensing, in addition to toy sales generated by Spin Master.

"老实说，作为犯罪剧的剧本，我感到有些不够尽兴。案件的解决在一定程度上依赖于巧合或登场人物的自我毁灭，通过调查积累产生的必然性较弱。矢吹的前搭档被杀的经过等，也留下了让人无法完全信服的点。此外，对石塚这个人物的刻画也让人感到违和。在进行惨绝人寰的谋杀的同时，他又会为孤儿们的未来担忧，低声下气地拜托别人照顾。残暴之人对特定对象展现温柔本身并非绝不自然。只是，他在两个场景中的表情相差太大，与其说是同一个人的两面性，看上去更像是在演截然不同的人物。虽然我对演员的表现感到不够满意，但这或许也是导演手法的问题。另一方面，小栗旬的演技非常精彩。尤其令人印象深刻的是矢吹使用毒品后自嘲般咕哝着“我在干什么呢”的场景。他明白自己正在堕落。却又无法停下。愚蠢与可怜共存的男人的悲凉，在那个短小的场景中凝聚了下来。失去前搭档的记忆以及反复对自己重复的“没关系”这句话，也成了思考其内心世界的线索。到了尾声，当矢吹接手照顾孤儿们时，我曾预感他最后大概不会背叛新搭档、会优先选择保护人的生命。然而，这种选择并不能一笔勾销过去的恶行。他的行为伴随着相应的责任。包含着这种严厉性在内，结局有让人信服的部分。作为犯罪剧的发展确实留下了不满。尽管如此，走向毁灭的男人的心理以及小栗旬所表现出的人性矛盾，还是深深吸引了我。故事的完成度与人物描写的魅力并不一定划等号。这是让我再次感受到这一点的作品。", ホーム > 作品情報 > 映画「バッド・ルーテナント：トウキョウ」

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

解説・あらすじ

三池崇史監督が小栗旬とリリー・ジェームズをメインキャストに迎え、ハリウッドと日本の共同プロジェクトとして製作されたサスペンスアクション。1992年のアメリカ映画「バッド・ルーテナント 刑事とドラッグとキリスト」をもとに、舞台を東京に移して再構築。小栗扮する悪徳刑事（バッド・ルーテナント）とジェームズ演じるFBI捜査官がバディを組み、街に渦巻く陰謀に立ち向かう姿を描く。 新宿・歌舞伎町の裏社会に生きる刑事・矢吹恭二は、ドラッグやギャンブルに溺れヤクザから命を狙われているうえに、相棒を殺したという噂まであった。彼が借金取りに追われる日々を過ごしていたある日、ヤクザを狙った連続猟奇殺人事件が発生。捜査に乗り出した矢吹は遺体の入れ墨から身元を特定し、石塚満という男が容疑者として浮上する。そんな中、矢吹は日本で行方不明になった次期アメリカ大統領の娘を捜索するため来日したFBI捜査官グエンとバディを組むことになる。矢吹が捜査する殺人事件とグエンの追う失踪事件は複雑に絡み合い、やがてある陰謀が浮かび上がる。 共演には、間宮祥太朗、野村周平、西野七瀬、向里祐香、岩田剛典、渡邊圭祐、中野英雄、村上淳、國村隼、舘ひろし、世界的人気を誇る女子プロレスラーのリブ・モーガンら豪華キャストが集結。Adoが主題歌を担い、楽曲制作にはグラミー賞受賞の世界的作曲家・宅見将典が参加。

title_original: Metamorfosi ed evoluzione nell’opera di Umico Niwa
editorial_title_zh: Umico Niwa作品中的 metamorphosis 与演进
editorial_excerpt_zh: 通过在罗马T293画廊推出的新书《Daphne》和展览《Daphne, Act Two》，Umico Niwa将蜕变转化为一种亲密的体验，在这里，身体与记忆的脆弱性开启了生存的新可能 L'articolo Metamorfosi ed evoluzione nell’opera di Umico…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Umico Niwa的新书《Daphne》中充满了抓拍照片、小型装置、各种艺术作品，以及一些随意的物品，例如一束鲜花、看起来几乎经历过太多次生命变化的毛绒玩具、在各处拍摄的几只动物、大量的自然风光以及艺术家认为有必要纳入其中的几个人物。这是一部亲密的合集，其间穿插着Umico本人所写的诗歌，书名刻意呼应了希腊神话中同名仙女的形象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一构筑回溯了她的生活以及被理解为转化和再生的改变概念，在罗马T293画廊举办的艺术家新展《Daphne, Act Two》中也清晰可见。这场个展分为两个大房间，延续了在各个衍生项目中被唤起和庆祝的演进：从最初的“Act One”（第一幕）空间开始，那里摆放着由有机材料和锡镴组成的形体；再到第二个区域“Act Two”（第二幕），其中的主体（在评论文本中也被称为达芙妮Daphnes）彼此互动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Umico-Niwa-Daphne-Act-Two-installation-view-at-T293-Photo-by-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-1024x665.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Umico Niwa《Daphne, Act Two》；T293画廊的展览现场。摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览中展出的作品与艺术家先前的创作保持着连贯性：带有各种花卉的枝桠被安放在远离自然环境的地方，靠近插座、微波炉或公寓中，如同缠绕在管道周围的攀援植物，或是从电表和悬挂在天花板上的灯具之间显现出来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "所选取的自然并非一成不变，它是多面的、色彩极其丰富的，有时甚至是烧焦的或局部干枯的，然而却从未给人以毫无生气或形同废弃的感觉。另一方面，在Umico看来，那些如同戏剧舞台角色般出现的达芙妮（Daphnes），也是以极大深度来应对个人经历（例如性别过渡）的工具，并认识到倾听新一代的重要性，尽管许多国家倒退政策的推进在很大程度上助长了暴力事件的不断增多。通过这场个展以及此前的书籍，Umico回想起了手术的那一天以及术后护理这一敏感主题，它们在《Daphne, Act Two》的布景现实中找到了宣泄口。因此，身体充当了各个元素（达芙妮Daphnes）与周围环境演进之间的黏合剂。参与这一“游戏”的人可以在虚构的条件下从内部采取行动，干涉对某个虚幻空间和时间的表现。达芙妮正是在这种视角中回归。在其著作中，Umico回忆了这一系列诞生时的时刻——即当她偶遇一尊描绘该仙女的雕像时，便感到了将金属熔入树枝模具的需求，并回忆起这正发生在一个复杂的时期，当时她正面对着“the loss of having children of my own, witnessing the death of a tree, and the passing of another transwoman in my community. Daphne was there for me when I needed the most”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Ph.-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-1-1024x675.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Umico Niwa, Newfound moon, 2026 (Daphne) foraged organic matter, brittania pewter, copper, fine silver, liver of sulfur, acrylic paint 5 × 7.5 × 5 cm Foto Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "达芙妮（Daphne）由此充当了黏合剂，而Umico嫁接在城市甚至往往是室内空间的嫩芽，在没有修辞的情况下，留下了期待感，部分带有希望，尽管它们同时也捕捉到了画廊大房间角落里可见的残骸中被唤起并简化的那种最初的绝望感。演进呈现为一个脆弱却顽强的过程，同时一种足以打破环境中不确定性痕迹的转变正在浮现。从这个意义上说，书中收录的一首诗具有重要意义，它写道：“If I could cast a ripple through space and time, so as to hold you both, see you once more”，这是对渴望的表达、对空间和时间所强加局限的超越，甚至也是对记忆及与过去事物联系的一种隐喻、对演进的新定义、对更广阔扩张感的表达，与此同时，这也是与自身生活过去版本清晰纯净的联系。", "translated": true}]
